At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive.
Lyft Urban Solutions powers the bike-sharing and scooter-sharing systems that move millions of people in over 60 cities worldwide. We built North America's first automated bike-share system and continue to lead the micromobility revolution.

Our systems operate globally - from Citi Bike in New York to BIXI in Montreal, Divvy in Chicago, Capital Bikeshare in DC, and iconic systems in Austin, Barcelona, Bogota, Boston, Buenos Aires, Columbus, Detroit, Dubai, London, Madrid, Mexico City, Monaco, Pittsburgh, Portland, Rio de Janeiro, San Francisco, Toronto, and beyond.
We're not just technology providers - we operate these systems, building the software, hardware, and operations that make urban micromobility work at scale.
Ready to shape how millions of people move through their cities every day?
We are looking for a passionate Product Designer to join our Montreal office to work on Lyft’s micromobility Operations Technology team.
As a member of the Operations Technology team, you’ll be responsible for evolving the platform that drives the global on-the-ground operations of our business. You’ll be designing features that are used in warehouses, vans, & on-the-ground to make our transportation systems some of the most reliable in the world. You’ll confront complex technical challenges & advocate for experiences that delight our operators and promote efficiency.
Our Montreal office developed the first automated bikes-share system in North America and continues to work on the platform today that provides state-of-the-art electric bikes and scooters for tens of millions of rides per year.
As a product designer at Lyft, you will be involved at every step of product development, from brainstorming broad ideas to ensuring design quality through launch. Using your full range of interaction, visual, and product thinking skills. As a product designer on the Lyft Urban Solutions team you will own the design of features within the core rider experience for our bike and scooter riders, within the Lyft app and our market specific apps.
In a lot of ways, we function as a startup, meaning we all work closely and collaboratively across organizations to align on product vision and ship products. Our Design and Research teams live and breathe a user-centered process to create the best possible, end-to-end, experience for riders all over the world. We can be scrappy when we need to be, though we are always focused on quality and influence.
As a qualified candidate, you have a track record of leading projects to successful outcomes for users and the business. You are a strong cross-functional partner, a great communicator, and are able to take a solution from idea to implementation. You uphold a high-quality bar and have a strong appreciation for the details. Above all, you approach problems holistically and create elegantly simple solutions to multi-faceted problems.

Plan strategically and think tactically as a partner with product and engineering to define the future of the team.
Influence the shape of the product with research and data while executing design work using high quality wireframes, mockups, user journeys, and cross-platform interactive prototypes.
Advocate for design by sharing your work and presenting cross-functionally, while being able to precisely articulate design rationale.
Inspire the entire team (including your cross-functional) partners by bringing new ideas to the table.
Create a unified, end-to-end experience through close collaboration with team members from across the Product and Marketing Design Teams.

Experience designing innovative products for desktop and mobile
Excellent oral and written communication skills
Experience with user research methods and analysis

Excellence in design craft
Ability to work with a low-ego, highly collaborative, cross-functional team
Excited about working in a fast-paced, dynamic startup environment

About the Opportunity
We're looking for a Product Designer to join N26's UX team in our Grow and Engage domain . There are a couple of areas within the domain where we're adding design strength, and we'll match you to the right one based on your background and what you're drawn to .
In this role, you'll work in the Grow & Engage domain—the heart of the cu stomer experience ranging from the acquisition and signup to our premium membership tiers and the daily engagement of our users . You will work in teams delivering the newest and most innovative features serving our custome rs in the best way possible .

You'll design end-to-end on important features and flows that millions of customers use every day . You'll report to our Head of UX, and work in a tight cross-functional team of product, engineering, research, and data partners .

We'll back you to grow your craft on work that matters—to customers, to the business, and to your own development as a designer .
We believe our team's diversity is our strength . The more perspectives at the table, the better . Please apply regardless of your identity, experience, or background .

We highly encourage you to attach your most recent portfolio and CV in English to your application.
Applications without a portfolio will not be considered
About the Work
The Grow and Engage domain is where we shape how customers get genuine, lasting value from N26 . It covers a broad slice of the core product—the moments that bring customers back to their day-to-day banking, the features that build habits and surface real value, and the way our paid tiers turn into something subscribers actively feel .
The work spans the home screen, in-app discovery, recommendations and AI-powered insights, the cross-cutting patterns that pull the whole product together, and our Smart, Go, and Metal subscription tiers—where the opportunity is to weave value through the product rather than bolt it on . You'll have meaningful scope to shape both how we package what we have today and what comes next .
You'll be designing for a fintech product used by millions, in a category where customers' expectations have been shaped by some of the best digital products in the world . The bar is high, and the work matters .

Design end-to-end on important features within your segment, from problem framing through research, exploration, and shipped work .
Bring a high bar for craft —UI and interaction design that delights customers and converts .
Frame design problems sharply : define user needs, success criteria, constraints, and tradeoffs before jumping into solutions .
Develop user flows and interactions that hold up across the connected parts of the product, anticipating how your work affects adjacent areas .
Contribute to our design system —using and improving the patterns the team relies on .
Be data-informed : plan and run research that blends qualitative and quantitative methods, and proactively seek out the data you need when it isn't on the table .
Partner closely with product, engineering, research, and data to ship work that actually lands—and to take it further once it's live .
Use AI tools fluently as part of your design practice—for exploration, prototyping, synthesis, and to accelerate the parts of the work that benefit from acceleration .

We pair tightly with PM and engineering to develop delightful, scalable solutions .
Hands-on leadership—managers still design .
AI is a real, ongoing part of how we work—across design tooling, prototyping, and product . We expect everyone on the team to be fluent and curious here .
We ship, and we ship often . We learn from what's live as much as from what's in Figma .

s.h: You're a good fit if you have
s.t:
A strong portfolio showing end-to-end product design work on consumer products—ideally mobile .
Experience taking complex feature work from problem to ship, owning the design throughout .
Experience working with a design system—using it, contributing to it, and knowing when to push back on it .
Experience grounding decisions in research and data—and a willingness to seek them out when they're not available .
Strong written and verbal communication—you can explain your decisions to product, engineering, and leadership .

Pride in quality : You sweat the details—interaction, visual, copy, edge cases—and you treat your craft as something you're actively growing .
Systems thinking : You see the connections between parts of a product, and you design with the wider experience in mind .
Problem-first mindset : You're rigorous about understanding the real problem, the real user, and the real constraints before committing to a direction .
Bias for action : You move fast, prototype to learn, and resist the pull of polishing in isolation .
AI-curious : You're active in using AI tools to extend what you can do and reshape your design practice .
Generous collaborator : You give and receive feedback well, and you're invested in making the work better—not just yours .

Accelerate your career growth by joining one of Europe's most talked about disruptors .
Employee benefits that range from a competitive personal development budget, work from home budget, discounts to fitness & wellness memberships, language apps and public transportation .
Premium banking services : As an N26 employee you will have access to a Premium subscription on your personal N26 bank account , as well as subscriptions for friends and family members .
Generous time off : Additional day of annual leave for each year of service .
Autonomy & culture : A high degree of autonomy and access to cutting-edge technologies—all while working with a friendly team of peers of diverse nationalities, life experiences, and family statuses .
Relocation support : A relocation package with visa support for those who need it .
Who We Are
N26 has reimagined banking for today's digital w orld . Technology and design empower everything we do—and it's how we are building the global banking platform the world loves to use . Founded in 2013, N26 serves over 7 million customers across 24 markets .

We've eliminated physical branches, paperwork, and hidden fees for an elegant digital experience and supreme savings . Giving people the power to live and bank their way is what gets us out of bed in the morning and inspires the work that we do .
Our UX team is part of the wider Product & UX organisation . We're a multidisciplinary group of 40 + designers, researchers, content designers , and design ops practitioners (we call ourselves "UXers"), most of us embedded in cross-functional product teams . Our team is base d in Berlin and Barcelona .
Sounds good? Apply now for this position .
Equal Opportu nities
We recognize that our strength lies in our people and the varied perspectives they bring to our workforce . We stri ve to build talented and diverse teams to drive our business success and empower our people to reach their full potential .
We genuinely welcome and encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, cultures, genders, sexual orientations, abilities, neurodiversities, and ages . We're committed to creating an inclusive workspace where everyone feels valued and respected, free from harassment and discrimination .

A career at Roblox means you’ll be working to shape the future of human interaction, solving unique technical challenges at scale, and helping to create safer, more civil shared experiences for everyone.

Define UX strategy and design direction for Roblox’s Ads Platform and tooling
Design and evolve complex, end-to-end experiences that help advertisers launch impactful campaigns and creators maximize their earning potential.

Contribute to design culture through mentorship, critique, and raising the bar for product thinking, systems thinking, and craft.

8+ years of experience in product design, with a proven track record of shipping consumer-facing, platform, or complex B2B products.

What We’re Building
Cello helps businesses turn their users into their best acquisition channel. Our product is the easiest way to embed user and partner referrals directly into the products you love to use. With just a few lines of code, a company is set up for hyper growth that runs on autopilot instead of spending money on ads.
Teams at Bolt, Miro, Typeform, VEED, and Descript already run their referral programs on Cello. which is proof that word-of-mouth can be engineered as a real growth channel, not being a nice to have.
We're a small, remote-first team that builds infrastructure that lives in other people's products . That means our bar for craft and attention to detail is exceptionally high.

Our UI has to feel native inside other people's products that we don't control, our components have to hold up wildly across different use cases, and our decisions get scrutinized by the world's best growth, design and engineering teams.

So in addition to caring deeply about how things look and feel, we need people who can think in systems, tracing how a decision plays out across different user segments and across levels of the product.

We're looking for a Senior Product Designer to work closely with our founding designer, product and engineering teams on the core Cello experience. You'll be involved in every aspect of the product design cycle and expected to take ownership of the work end-to-end.
This role is fully remote but your work schedule needs to overlap comfortably with a European work day. We're an async-first culture that values deep focused work, but we still make time to get together in person at regular team off-sites.

Partner directly with our founding designer, product and engineering teams to take projects on our roadmap from rough problem to shipped solution.

Help define and improve our evolving design system.
Bring our brand to life across marketing, social and launch content.
Design mockups and prototypes in low and high fidelity to communicate ideas and how things might work.
Be part of and contribute to a growing design culture that's still taking shape.
Sweat the details that make embedded UI feel trustworthy.

Systems thinking: you can design components and patterns while thinking about how they fit into the broader system, but you also know when to push past convention and innovate.
Courage to challenge ideas, try new things and push a product direction forward.
Fluency designing in Figma and other prototyping tools. You also experiment regularly with new tooling.

Senior Product Designer @ Secfix
Location: Remote (EMEA) · CET/CEST timezone
Hi — I'm Grigory, co-founder and CTO at Secfix.
How do you feel about owning a feature from the first customer conversation to the version that's live on production — writing the spec yourself, pairing closely with engineers through the build, and overseeing your design shipped on production exactly the way you designed it? If that sounds like the right shape of the job — designer who owns, not designer who hands off — read on.
I've spent most of my career believing the best designers aren't the ones with the prettiest Figma files. They're the ones who can frame a problem, write a spec, sit with engineers through the build, and own that what shipped is what they designed. Our founding product designer, Ghada , has been doing exactly that since we started.

The engineering team has doubled and we're shipping faster than we ever have. We're hiring the second designer because there's more good work to do than one person can hold — and we'd rather ship twice as much than slow down.
Why Secfix exists
Over 1.78 million SMBs in Europe need to comply with security frameworks — ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, SOC 2 — just to sell to enterprise customers. The process is manual, painful, and takes over a year. We automated it.
Our platform integrates with a company's full tech stack — AWS, Azure AD, Jira, GitLab, GCP, and more — automatically extracts compliance evidence, and guides teams to certification in weeks instead of months. Our fastest customer certified in 4 weeks instead of the industry-standard 12+ months.
We've raised €17M in total (€12M Series A), backed by Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank), and Bayern Capital. We're on a profitable trajectory, growing fast, and building the team that will take us to European market leadership.
This space is not threatened by AI, it's amplified by it. Compliance requires deep domain expertise combined with automation. Our new AI product (CISO AI) is just getting started, and there's a huge amount of product design work ahead: agentic workflows, intelligent evidence collection, context-aware policy generation, and more.
What we believe
Compliance software has historically been built like the audit it automates — heavy, defensive, ugly. We're building something else. The customer is a real person trying to ship audit-ready evidence on a Friday afternoon. The product should respect their time, automate the boring parts, and make the rest feel calm.
Quality is the product. Most of our category competes on feature lists. We compete on craft. A clear empty state, a sync that doesn't lie, a settings page that holds together at eleven permission tiers — these are the things customers feel before they can name them. Design at Secfix is not what wraps the product. It's most of what makes it work.

We expect strong design skill, strong product thinking, and the ability to hold your own in a technical discussion. You work in a small team — usually with one or two engineers — and pair closely from the first prototype through to production. You own the project from beginning to end.
Alongside the features you ship, you do three things that make everyone else faster:
Maintain the components and patterns that make design fast.
Own how the team ships. We have no PMs. You write the specs, run the ticketing workflow, keep engineers unblocked.
Build the tools and skills — Cursor rules, design QA skills, prompt templates — that let engineers do good design work without you in the room.
The leverage is doing all four well. Doing only one is the wrong shape.
How we work
No PMs. Designers and engineers run product. You talk to customers, frame the problem, write the spec, decide what ships.
Small temporary teams. You plus one or two engineers per project. Whoever is closest to the problem leads.
Design leads the logic, engineering tests feasibility. You bring the V1. Engineers push back on what's expensive or risky, start ahead with system design. They help spot edge cases. You adjust it fast. We get from v1 to v4 in matter of hours or few days.
Prototype-grade, not wireframes. Real components, real states, real copy. Sometimes an LLM-built prototype before Figma. The component library stays current because the speed of design depends on it.
Handoff is the beginning, not the end. You're in the engineering channel. You review the PR. You verify on production. Staging QA is the first gate, not the last.
In-sync culture with thoughtful coms mindset. Loom for reviews, Notion for specs, quick loops in Gather where written coms doesn’t cut it, all happening in the same time zone. Team mates are reviewing things quick. Engineers and designers spend under two hours weekly meetings.
AI is part of the craft. We use Claude to pressure-test ideas, draft specs, surface edge cases, write test cases. Not to skip thinking.
The first three months
Month 1. Ship your first design to production. Get into the codebase, the customer language, the way we write specs. Sit on customer calls.
Month 2. Own a full feature end-to-end. Customer conversations, problem framing, Figma, spec, engineer pairing, PR review, production verification.
Month 3 and beyond. Push the design system forward. Start building the tools and skills that make engineers faster at design. Improve the product design process. The bar is yours to defend.

8+ years designing B2B SaaS desktop applications as Staff/Principal Product Designer or similar. Dense interfaces — tables, filters, permissions, settings pages.
You've been the only designer, or one of two or three, in companies under 50 people at least once before. You know how to set the bar without a design org behind you.
Your portfolio is "I," not "we." You can name the engineer you paired with on each feature, the design decision you defended through the build, and what happened when the feature reached users.
You communicate clearly and concise in English: in Slack, in docs and on a call.
You're fast in Figma with or without AI. You’re already in a serious relationship with LLMs.
You treat engineering feasibility as input, not constraint. When an engineer says "three weeks, here's why," you find the version that's 80% as good and ships next week.
You're comfortable doing product work without the PM title.
You hear feedback and come back the next day with something better. You don't spend the hour in between defending the version that's already outdated.

The design challenges at Built are genuinely complex: the lenders, owners, developers, and contractors using our platform are navigating high-stakes financial workflows where clarity, accuracy, and trust are not nice-to-haves — they are requirements.

Be Bold. We pursue the biggest problems in our industry, challenge assumptions others take for granted, and take calculated risks to get there. We don’t hide behind consensus or committees. Playing it safe is just failing slowly.

Help Customers Win. We learn our customers’ businesses deeply — how they think, how they deploy capital, what keeps them up at night. We treat their capital like our own. We ship leverage, not features. And we measure ourselves by customer results, not our intentions.

Move with Urgency & Purpose. We bias toward delivery over perfection, remove friction from our own paths, and communicate in real time. Momentum compounds — and we build it every day.

Own the Outcome. We own outcomes, not just tasks. We hold a high Say:Do ratio and take responsibility from idea through impact. When something breaks, we fix it — we don’t wait to be asked.

Never Satisfied. We raise the bar continuously. We stay curious, hold exacting standards, debate hard, and hold our opinions loosely when the evidence shifts. Excellence is a habit, not an event.

About Bonusly
Bonusly is the recognition and rewards platform people actually use. We believe culture is built by everyone, not assigned by HR. When the whole team shows up for each other, something powerful happens: culture you can see, measure, and strengthen. Our AI companion, Bizy, helps people recognize each other better and helps leaders understand what's really happening across their organization.To learn more about working at Bonusly , check out our Un-Handbook:
Why this role exists
Our Insights business unit is one of our biggest bets: turning recognition data into strategic intelligence that helps leaders understand team health, engagement, and culture in real time. We're building AI-powered products (generative UIs, conversational analysis, culture visualizations) that surface patterns no survey could capture. The design conventions don't exist yet. We have to invent them.
The gap we're filling is creative energy. We're looking for someone who stretches us visually with fresh, imaginative ideas and a consumer sensibility that makes B2B software feel alive. You'll work alongside a product leader, an engineering leader, and another designer who leads the Insights BU, while collaborating with designers and engineers across the company.

Design AI-powered culture intelligence products from scratch: collaboration maps, engagement spotlights, organizational health dashboards. The UI has to earn trust
Shape product strategy with your product and engineering partners. You won't wait for specs. You'll help figure out what to build and why
Lead end-to-end design: research, flows, prototypes, high-fidelity visuals, and close collaboration with engineers through implementation
Bring a visual point of view. Push the craft through motion, illustration, layout, and thoughtful detail
Ship fast in ambiguity. Sometimes you lead with a concept, sometimes you refine an engineer's first pass. Designers here are partners from the first commit
Experiment with how Bizy shows up across the experience, from conversational interfaces to proactive insights that feel helpful, not intrusive
Design and AI at Bonusly
AI is changing what it means to be a designer. What the tools can't do is decide what's worth building, what feels right, and what will make someone pause. That's taste, and it's what we value most. We use AI tools daily and want someone with the judgment to know where they help and where they don't.
You're a great fit if you…
Have 5+ years of product design experience with a portfolio that shows range across UX thinking, visual craft, and interaction design
Have a creative streak beyond clean UI: illustration, motion, brand work, or side projects that show visual imagination
Can take complex, data-rich problems and make them feel simple and intuitive. Not by hiding complexity, but by designing through it
Have experience designing 0-to-1 products, especially in AI-powered environments where you had to invent the interface
Bring a consumer sensibility to B2B. You know what makes software feel good to use, not just functional
Have strong communication skills. You can make the case for a direction and bring people along
Are curious about AI as both a product space and a set of tools reshaping how you work

Experience with data visualization, analytics products, or culture/HR tech
Comfort prototyping in code (HTML/CSS/JS, React) or a genuine desire to learn. Our stack makes it easy
Experience designing conversational or AI-native interfaces
A few things to know
Will I have a design manager who knows design?
Yes. You'll report to the VP of Product & Design, who has a design background and leads our product design and marketing team. Design leadership here isn't an afterthought. It's how decisions get made.
Is this fully remote?
Yes. But we sell culture for a living, so we're our own best example: weekly creative warm ups, a design guild that brings product and marketing designers together, regular play sessions, and intentional team travel.

As a Product Designer at Maze, you'll define what product design looks like for AI agents in cybersecurity — a problem space where the design patterns don't exist yet. This is an early-hire role at a well-funded Series A startup building at the intersection of generative AI and security, and you'll own the product surface end-to-end while working directly with our Head of Product, engineering, and founders.
The product challenge is genuinely new. Our AI agents investigate vulnerabilities autonomously, surface findings with real context, and collaborate with security teams to cut through noise. Your job is to design how humans and agents work together — how trust gets built, how decisions get communicated, how complex security workflows become understandable. There's no playbook for this. You'll create one.
This role suits someone who operates closer to a product director than a screen-shipper — driving direction, influencing strategy, and making business-impact calls, alongside the visual craft to deliver them.

You'll be using AI tools daily to move faster, but your craft is the floor: every design choice should hold up on its own merits, independent of how it was generated.

Success looks like a design system shipped and adopted across the product, and concrete product outcomes — feature adoption, POC-to-customer conversion, and customer satisfaction with the experiences you ship.

Define AI-Agent UX Patterns: Design how security teams collaborate with autonomous AI agents — how investigations get presented, how trust is established, how humans steer the agent without slowing it down. You're inventing patterns, not applying existing ones.
Drive Product Direction, Not Just Design: Operate as a product-led designer — shaping roadmap, challenging requirements, influencing leadership with research and business reasoning. The bar is "what should we build, and why" alongside "how should it look."
Own the Product Surface End-to-End: Take features from problem framing through shipped product, working in tight partnership with PMs and engineers — including backend. Run discovery, prototype rapidly, validate with customers, and stay close to implementation. No throwing designs over the wall, no shipping around the engineering team.
Build the Design System: Create and scale a component-based design system that becomes the foundation for everything we ship. Establish patterns for AI-human collaboration that the team can build on as we grow.
Pioneer AI-Assisted Design Workflows: Use AI tools to accelerate ideation, prototyping, and exploration — and develop the methodologies the rest of the team will adopt. Your daily workflow is itself a contribution.
Translate Research Into Design: Run customer research, talk to security teams directly, and turn what you learn into shipped product. Use AI-assisted analysis to move from insight to prototype in days, not weeks.
Set the Quality Bar: Establish what "good" looks like for product design at Maze across craft, consistency, and customer impact — as the foundation for a design team that scales behind you.

s.h: What You Need to Be Successful
s.t:
Visual Craft for Data-Dense UI: A portfolio that holds up to detailed scrutiny — strong colour theory, deliberate visual hierarchy, considered information architecture for complex workflows. This is the bar, not a nice-to-have. Your interview will dig into specific design choices and why you made them.
Product Design Track Record: 4-7 years of professional product design experience, with shipped work in B2B SaaS. We're flexible on years; demonstrated craft and clear ownership matter more than time served.
Data-Heavy B2B Interfaces: Direct experience designing for complex workflows, dense data, and technical audiences. Dashboards, investigation tools, developer products, security platforms — the kind of UI where information density and decision support actually matter.
AI as Tool, Not Crutch: You use AI tools (Figma AI, Cursor, v0, Midjourney, ChatGPT/Claude, etc.) as part of your daily workflow and can speak credibly to what they're good for and where they break down. Critically, every design choice you ship should hold up on its own — AI accelerates your work, it doesn't substitute for foundational craft.
Product-Strategic Thinking: Track record of driving product direction, not just executing on briefs. You've influenced what to build with research, framed problems for leadership, and made business-impact calls — ideally in environments where you operated without a dedicated PM.
Deep Engineering Collaboration: Demonstrable history of shipping work in tight partnership with engineers — including backend. Pairing on implementation, working in design tokens, understanding the systems your designs land in, building consensus rather than shipping around resistance.
Design Systems Experience: Background building or meaningfully contributing to a design system in a production product. You think in components, tokens, and patterns, not one-off screens.
Customer-Led Approach: Comfortable running discovery directly with users, synthesising what you hear, and using that to make calls about what to build. You don't wait for research to be handed to you.

Experience designing for cybersecurity, developer tools, or other technical product domains
Background designing agentic or AI-native product experiences (not just AI features bolted onto existing products)
Early-stage startup experience where you've operated without a manager or established design function

Define a New Design Space: AI agents in security is a genuinely new problem. The interaction patterns, trust models, and workflows don't exist yet — you'll create them. The work you do here will influence how this entire category gets designed.
Fast-Track to Design Leadership: This is a founding-trajectory role and we're hiring for someone who wants a long-term home, not a stepping stone. As the team scales, the natural path is IC → Lead → Head of Design. If you have leadership ambitions, you'll have the runway to grow into them. If you'd rather stay deeply hands-on, the IC scope grows with the product.
Ambitious Challenge: We're using generative AI (LLMs and agents) to solve one of the most pressing problems in cybersecurity — the gap between vulnerability findings and meaningful action. You'll be designing at the cutting edge of this field.
Expert Team: Work alongside hands-on leaders with experience in Big Tech and Scale-ups. Our team has been part of the leadership teams behind multiple acquisitions and an IPO.
Impactful Work: Cybersecurity is a force for good. The experiences you design will directly affect how security teams protect organisations worldwide.
Build an AI-Native Company: We're building a new company in the AI era with the opportunity to design everything from the ground up — including how the design function itself works. You'll help pioneer AI-assisted design practices and set new standards.

Hi! I'm Chris , head of Product Design at Ashby.
We're looking for a versatile, intrinsically motivated designer who is excited to contribute to rethinking how modern software is designed. At Ashby, you'll be part designer, part product manager, part consultant, and part design system manager (or some combination of the 4!). We do design differently here, and if that excites you, read on.
Our unique approach is working - we're growing >100% year-over-year and have notable customers like Notion, Linear, Shopify, and Snowflake. Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, very low churn, and many years of runway. We're backed by amazing investors like Y Combinator, Elad Gil, Lachy Groom, and many more! We’ll share more details once we meet.
How We Work
In my previous roles, product teams always consisted of a product manager, a designer, and ~4-5 engineers. This may sound familiar to you! The product manager briefs the designer who then designs. After designing, mocks are handed to the engineers.
We take a more principled approach here at Ashby. If you've been designing software enough, you'll realize in actuality, design is required in varying degrees on each project.

Sometimes in the past, I'd be asked to design yet another settings page, when really all that was needed was an engineer to reuse existing components and just follow some documentation I had written. Other times, I felt I should effectively be the product manager and own a project from beginning to end.

In these latter cases, it made sense that I was even the one providing project updates and managing resources rather than constantly being pinged by a separate product manager.
This principled approach is now what we do here, and it is part of what has allowed Ashby to take down incumbents in multiple verticals all at once. We don't settle for the status quo—we actively resist reversion to the mean.
Currently, I report to Benji, the co-founder & CEO. Both Abhik and Benji (our founders) care deeply about design, which at first glance may seem counterintuitive given the number of full-time designers that we employ. The belief is not that design is unimportant, but rather that it should be owned by the product team collectively, not solely by a group of full-time designers who happen to have the job title.
The design department’s job at Ashby is not to make every single design decision but to equip our entire product team to make better decisions themselves, as well as edit decisions that PMs/Engineers choose to make. That, while tackling the biggest design challenges ourselves.
Separate from design, you may also be excited by the fact that we maintain a near seed-stage-like culture with fuzzy lines between functional roles, as much autonomy as you can handle, and a focus on IC-work with an almost-no-meeting culture. While you get the product-market fit and scale of a growth-stage startup, you also get the agency and no-nonsense, no-red-tape culture of a seed-stage startup.
What We’re Building
Talent teams aspire to build a hiring process that identifies great candidates, moves them quickly through the interview process, and provides an excellent experience for the candidate. To accomplish this, recruiters perform thousands of daily tasks to coordinate and relay information between candidates, interviewers, and hiring managers. Teams struggle to keep up!
Scheduling a final round is an excellent example of our customers' challenges.

A recruiter needs to collect availability from the candidate, identify potential interviewers, perform “Calendar Tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and perform any last-minute adjustments as availability changes.

They must perform this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others.
Ashby provides talent teams with intelligent and powerful software that provides insights into where they’re failing and automates or simplifies many of the tasks they’re underwater with. We put a lot of effort into designing products that are approachable to beginners but mastered and extended by power users. In many ways, spreadsheets set the bar here (and are what we often replace!).
Why you should or shouldn’t apply

4+ years of product design experience in desktop SaaS.
Able to think from first principles instead of simply applying the “standard” UX processes.
Can break down complex user problems by asking questions that narrow down the solution space.
Enough experience that your intuition can solve many usability problems without having to rely solely on data & metrics or conducting user research.
Curious & resourceful enough to come up with creative solutions and de-risk them appropriately.
Strong skills in layout, navigation, IA, UI, and interaction design.
Strong visual design skills and obsession with craft & details.
As a bonus, you have experience at an early-stage startup or have spent time as a solo designer on a team.

s.h: You may want to apply if you’re excited about
s.t:
Creating leverage and impact far and above what you'd see in a typical EPD product team structure. You won’t be a cog in the wheel, the wheel is not very big!
Getting to work on all parts of a massive product surface area - spanning many user types, JTBDs, usability challenges, etc. Unlike in other organizations, you won’t be stuck working on one problem for many years.
Helping reinvent the design model for modern enterprise software—you don’t have to build wireframes, user journeys, personas, etc. What matters is solving a customer’s problem; what tools you use are up to you.
Covering all parts of the design process with a focus on design craft. You'll still be doing the occasional user research interview but will be focused on using heuristics & experience to improve our IA, navigation, interactions, UI patterns, and more.
Helping build our design system from (almost) the ground up.

s.h: Conversely, you may not want to apply if
s.t:
You feel uncomfortable designing independently without much guidance from a PM or design management.
You’re uncomfortable having your decisions and process being challenged constantly by engineering & product.
You prefer an in-person role over remote (Ashby operates remotely).
You dislike written documentation.
You want a set structure and rhythm to your projects.
PM gives you a brief, you do wireframes, then mocks, then pass off work to engineers. Rinse and repeat.
You prefer a narrow job scope - interaction design only, design system only , etc.

s.h: On a weekly basis you will find yourself
s.t:
Consulting for engineers who need help structuring layout, typography, flows, etc.
Digging into problems by consulting GTM, talking to customers, asking for data requests, and more in order to present confident assumptions about your proposals.
Using Figma to draw out your ideas and create visual artifacts for stakeholder alignment.
Writing specification docs (we call them specs!) that detail your design proposals. These documents are meant to get stakeholder alignment on the biggest decisions you want to make and are a core part of how we work at Ashby.

In 1954, architect Eero Saarinen designed a radically modern bank branch for Irwin Union in Columbus, Indiana. With glass walls, no private offices, and a floor plan that invited openness, it embodied a new kind of transparency in finance. The building was surrounded by trees, furnished by Herman Miller, and featured rustic brick flooring. Today, that space is a conference center, and that spirit of design-forward thinking in banking* feels all but extinct.
Mercury believes that level of care and craft in design has been lost in modern finance, and we’re building products that bring it back. Cards and credit are built on complicated systems and inherited conventions, but our customers shouldn’t have to experience that complexity. We believe thoughtful design can turn something traditionally transactional into an experience that feels simple, intuitive, and distinctly Mercury .
We’re looking for a Senior Product Designer to join our Cards & Credit team. You’ll tackle complex product problems, question inherited assumptions, and shape experiences that help startups spend less time banking and more time building.

Own meaningful Cards & Credit product problems from initial framing through shipped experience, partnering closely with Product and Engineering to understand the problem and shape what we should build.
Turn complicated systems, requirements, and edge cases into experiences that feel remarkably simple and intuitive.
Work across the entire design stack, from framing problems and exploring concepts to workflows, detailed interactions, visual design, prototyping, and final implementation.
Explore broadly and design from first principles, questioning inherited patterns and assumptions when a better answer may exist.
Bring a high level of interaction and visual craft to the Cards & Credit experience, from the structure of a workflow to the details of hierarchy, typography, motion, and state.
Collaborate with Mercury ’s Brand team on physical cards and related products, creating a cohesive experience between the objects our customers hold and the product experiences surrounding them.
Develop a deep understanding of our customers, communicate the reasoning behind your decisions clearly, and work through tradeoffs with your partners to arrive at the strongest solution.

A strong portfolio of product work demonstrating exceptional product thinking, interaction design, and visual craft.
An ability to understand complicated systems and turn them into simple, thoughtful product experiences.
Deep curiosity about why a problem exists before deciding how to solve it, with a willingness to question assumptions and work from first principles.
Real ambition for the work itself. You want to do the best work of your career here, and you’re energized by being surrounded by people who hold themselves to the same bar.
A high bar for craft and the judgment to know where additional thought and detail meaningfully improve an experience.
Comfort navigating ambiguity and taking ownership without waiting for every requirement to be defined.
A habit of exploring multiple possibilities, prototyping ideas, and changing direction when a stronger solution emerges.
Strong communication and collaboration skills, including the ability to articulate your thinking, explain tradeoffs, and build conviction with Product and Engineering partners.
Deep care for customers and an ambition to create products that don’t just function well, but genuinely make their lives better.
You don’t need a background in banking, fintech, cards, or credit. We care much more about whether you’ve demonstrated the ability to understand complicated problems and turn them into simple, thoughtful product experiences.
Complexity can be learned. The instinct to find its essence is harder to teach.

We're looking for a Product Designer to help shape the shared experiences and systems that connect Hudl's products.
Hudl is bringing together products used across sports, teams and organizations into a more connected platform. That creates design problems that don't always fit neatly within a single feature or product: how information is structured, how common workflows behave across products, how video and data work together, and how emerging technologies like AI change the way people interact with Hudl.
You'll work within Core UX, the team responsible for the design foundations that help Hudl's products feel clear, consistent and connected. Our work includes shared patterns and experiences, information architecture, video and data, and the systems that help product teams build at scale.

Solve connected problems. You'll work on experiences that cross features, products and workflows, considering how individual design decisions fit into the broader Hudl platform.
Make complexity easier to understand. You'll turn complicated workflows, information and technical constraints into experiences that feel clear and intuitive.
Work across teams. You'll partner with product, engineering and other designers to understand problems, explore solutions and help create experiences that can work at scale.
Design from evidence. You'll learn directly from customers, use research and product data to inform your work, and test and iterate on ideas as you go.
Own your work through delivery. You'll independently run scoped design projects, working from early exploration through implementation and measuring how well the solution works once it's shipped.
For this role, we're currently considering candidates who are within commuting distance of our offices in London, but we're also open to remote candidates in the U.K.
Must-Haves
Strong product design craft. You can turn complex requirements into clear, intuitive experiences through strong interaction and visual design. You know how to choose the right methods and level of fidelity for the problem, moving between exploration, prototyping and delivery.
Systems thinking. You're comfortable working through ambiguity, naturally look for connections, and consider how a solution might affect other workflows, users or parts of a product.
Collaborative communication. You can explain your thinking, seek out feedback and work through different perspectives with product, engineering and design partners.
Customer and evidence focus. You're comfortable talking with customers and using research, product data and other evidence to make and evaluate design decisions.
AI fluency. You actively use AI tools in your design process and are curious about how AI changes the products we design. You're comfortable experimenting with emerging interaction patterns and thinking critically about where AI can improve an experience.
A strong portfolio. You can show how you've worked through product problems, including your reasoning, collaboration and iteration rather than only the final solution.

Experience with complex or connected products. You’ve designed experiences that span multiple workflows, surfaces or parts of a larger product, and understand how individual design decisions contribute to a cohesive experience.
Experience with data-rich or technical products. You’ve designed products involving complex data, analytics, video or other technically challenging workflows.
Experience with design systems or information architecture. You’ve worked with shared patterns, design systems, information architecture or other foundations that help experiences scale across a product.
AI product design experience. You’ve designed conversational, agentic or other AI-powered experiences and have explored emerging interaction patterns beyond traditional interfaces.

Cover your medical insurance . We have multiple plans to pick from to ensure you’ll have the coverage you (and your dependents) want, including vision, dental, fertility healthcare and family forming benefits.

Communication. Clear, specific, opinionated. You say what you decided and why, and you are just as clear on what you chose not to do and why.

LLMs are already embedded in your workflow.

Problem definition. Break it down. Package it back up.

Collaborative creation. You work well across product, engineering and clinical, and you know a good idea can come from any of them. You listen to feedback and take it on, using it to make the work better.

Berlin-based or willing to relocate.

This role is about designing experiences that perform. You’ll work at the intersection of user behavior, data, and business goals, shaping flows that drive engagement and revenue. At exmox, we're also embracing AI as part of how we work, not just what we build. We use AI tools to work smarter, cut down on repetitive tasks and spend our time where it actually moves the needle. If that mindset speaks to you, you'll fit right in.
Our product design team is growing in maturity, and you’ll play a key role in shaping how design works at exmox. If you want high impact, real ownership, and a product at scale, we want to hear from you.

Research collaboration: Work closely with UX research and data teams to evaluate and improve your designs.

What’s in it for you as a designer? Impact : Your work directly influences a product used by millions. You’ll see the effect of your design decisions on business KPIs and learn how to create value through design.
Data-driven culture : Data sits at the core of every decision we make. You’ll design, test, and iterate based on real user insights and performance metrics.
Large global user base : You’ll design for a product with over 25 million users worldwide, operating at true scale.
Growing design maturity : Our product design team is on a journey to elevate design maturity at exmox, and you’ll actively shape and contribute to that evolution.
Cross-functional design team : You’ll collaborate within a dedicated design team including Product designers, UI Designers, and UX Researcher.

Professional experience: 5+ years of experience working in product teams as a UI, UI/UX, or Product Designer.
Consumer product design: Experience designing habit-forming, engaging, consumer-facing interfaces.
Industry background: Experience in marketing, gaming, or other B2C-heavy industries is a plus.
Hard Skills: Design tools: Strong proficiency in Figma.
Motion & interaction design: Expertise in motion design, animation, and transitions to craft dynamic interfaces.
Visual asset creation: Expertise in creating illustrations, iconography, and other visual assets.
Design systems: Expertise in designing, shipping, and maintaining design systems.
Multi-brand products: Experience with multi-brand, white-label products and theming systems.
Brand identity: Experience in defining, designing, and documenting brand identities.
Copywriting: Experience in copywriting, including defining tone, voice, and messaging.
Accessibility & usability: Strong knowledge of accessibility and usability principles.
Frontend awareness: Understanding of front-end technologies and implementation constraints.
Language skills: Fluency in English; German is a plus.
Soft Skills: Ownership : You take full responsibility for your work, drive initiatives forward, align stakeholders, and ensure meaningful value delivery.
Proactiveness : You anticipate challenges, identify opportunities, and take initiative without waiting for direction.
Prioritisation : You focus on what matters most, balance speed and quality, and manage your workload effectively in a fast-paced environment.
Feedback mindset : You give constructive feedback thoughtfully and embrace feedback as an essential part of iteration and growth, comfortably navigating multiple refinement cycles.
Creative thinking : You explore a wide range of ideas and solutions from safe bets to bold, out-of-the-box concepts to achieve the most impactful outcome.
How We Win Speed is the feature. Speed beats rocket science. We move fast, test fast, and multiply our pace with AI, because action creates information and small wins compound. A fast failure is a lesson we learn from, a slow one is a problem we can't afford.
Focus on the essential. Done is better than perfect. We stay focused on what actually moves us forward and protect people's time from anything that doesn't. We're direct in how we communicate too, no rambling, no unnecessary detail.
See it. Own it. Solve it. The first to see it is best placed to fix it. We're not a place for comfort, we're a place for doers. "Not my job" isn't in our vocabulary, if you spot something, you help make sure it gets solved.
Respect others. Trust multiplies. Respect is non-negotiable. We disagree with ideas, never with people. Trust here is built the same way it is anywhere, through consistency, a thank you, a moment of listening, and owning your mistakes.
Perks that help you focus on what matters. Transport subsidy, learning budget, wellness and gym, workation, bi-weekly team lunches, and more. The perks are great, but the real reason people join and stay is the challenge, the ownership, and the drive to win together.

Prototype in real code environments and shape the future of design/engineering collaboration.
Help build an AI-accelerated design workflow that’s growing and evolving quickly.

Edelman is a voice synonymous with trust, reimagining a future where the currency of communication is action. Our culture thrives on three promises: boldness is possibility, empathy is progress, and curiosity is momentum.

We are in relentless pursuit of an equitable and inspiring workplace that is respectful of all, reflects and represents the world in which we live, and fosters trust, collaboration and belonging.

Edelman AI is seeking a Product Designer, Mid Level, to help shape clear, consistent experiences across our internal platform that brings together insights, content creation, and proprietary AI tools into one shared environment for teams.
This is an end-to-end product design role, not a UI-only role. You will independently own design workstreams from Discovery through Evaluation, including lightweight research, problem framing, ideation, end-to-end flows, high-fidelity UI, design system execution, delivery partnership, and UX QA.
You will partner closely with Product Owners, engineers, and stakeholders to translate complex capabilities into human-centered experiences that are usable, accessible, and scalable across teams. You will work within an established Design System and an AI-assisted development workflow, and your job is to execute within them with precision while flagging gaps and contributing documentation that keeps the system healthy.
What success looks like
You can take an ambiguous problem and drive it from framing to shipped solution, proactively aligning with the UX Lead at key decision moments
You reduce rework by surfacing risks early and designing complete end-to-end flows, including edge cases and states, not just happy paths
You keep consistency across squads by defaulting to existing patterns and contributing improvements
You collaborate smoothly with engineers and Product Owners, keeping decisions crisp and documented
You follow through after release, validating outcomes and feeding learnings back into future work

Insight-Led Product Development
Drive problem framing with Product Owners, including primary users, jobs to be done, constraints, assumptions, and risks
Plan and run lightweight research activities when needed, such as quick interviews, concept checks, and usability tests
Synthesize findings into clear recommendations that influence solution direction
Define success signals during Discovery and support evaluation after release by comparing outcomes to those signals
Rapid Concepting and Holistic Experience Design
Generate multiple solution directions quickly and articulate tradeoffs in plain language
Prototype at the right fidelity, starting with quick and lightweight concepts, to align stakeholders and reduce risk before build
Deliver end-to-end flows that include key states and edge cases
Ensure usability best practices are applied consistently across the experience
Design System-Led Craft
Design polished high-fidelity UI aligned with brand guidelines and our Design System
Default to existing patterns and reuse components consistently across squads
When a clear gap exists, document it with variants, states, and usage guidance and raise it with the UX Lead for review before extending the system
Ensure responsive behavior and accessibility basics are included from the start
Embedded Engineering Partnership
Collaborate early with engineers on feasibility, scope, and technical constraints before designs are considered final
Specify behaviors precisely, including interactions, content requirements, states, and responsive rules
Keep handoff current during build and communicate changes clearly to the rest of the squad
Support implementation by answering questions quickly and helping unblock delivery
Quality Ownership from Design to Release
Verify the built experience across key screens, browsers, and breakpoints
Write clean bug reports with clear repro steps and expected versus actual behavior, including screenshots
Capture learnings post-release and feed improvements back into patterns and future work

3 to 5 years of Product Design experience, including owning work from Discovery through Delivery
Portfolio demonstrating problem framing, research-informed decisions, multiple options explored, and at least one end-to-end shipped workflow
Strong knowledge of Design Systems, including applying and evolving component libraries, documenting usage guidelines, and collaborating on governance so patterns stay consistent across squads
Strong proficiency in Figma, including component creation, variants, auto layout, and clean file structure
Comfort working alongside AI-assisted design and development workflows, including tools like Claude, and an understanding of how design decisions are consumed by AI agents in the build process
Proven ability to operate with ambiguity, take ownership, and deliver while proactively aligning with the UX Lead at key milestones
Familiarity with Mixpanel or similar analytics tools, and ability to combine quantitative signals with qualitative research insights to guide decisions
Strong collaboration and communication skills with Product and Engineering
High attention to detail and strong follow-through to ensure quality in the shipped experience

Understanding of communications and PR agency workflows, and how firms like Edelman operate across clients, teams, and delivery models
We are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your experience doesn’t perfectly align with every qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

About Decagon
Decagon is the leading conversational AI platform empowering every brand to deliver concierge customer experiences.
Our technology enables industry-defining enterprises like Avis Budget Group, Block’s Cash App and Square, Chime, Oura Health, and Hunter Douglas to deploy AI agents that power personalized, deeply satisfying interactions across voice, chat, email, SMS, and every other channel.
We’re building a future where customer experiences are being redefined from support tickets and hold music to faster resolutions, richer conversations, and deeper relationships. We’re proud to be backed by world-class investors who share that vision, including a16z, Accel, Bain Capital Ventures, Coatue, and Index Ventures, along with many others.
We’re an in-office company, driven by a shared commitment to excellence and velocity. Our values — Just Get It Done, Invent What Customers Want, Winner’s Mindset, and The Polymath Principle — shape how we work and grow as a team.

Decagon is the leading conversational AI platform, empowering every brand to deliver concierge customer experiences. Industry-defining enterprises like Cash App, Square, Chime, Oura, Delta Airlines, Tickemaster, American Airlines, and Avis use our platform to deploy AI agents that power personalized, deeply satisfying interactions across voice, chat, email, SMS, and every other channel.
We believe businesses deserve better, more human ways to care for their customers, and that AI finally makes that possible. Design at Decagon is early and growing.

You'd report to our Senior Director of Product Design and join a high-visibility, high-ownership team where your work directly shapes the product, the company, and the interaction patterns an entire industry is still figuring out.

We work across every customer segment, partnering closely with engineering, product, and go-to-market to make our platform robust, scalable, and easy to use.

Today, enterprises use Decagon to deploy AI agents that handle millions of customer conversations. Where we're headed is bigger: making those agents something teams can shape, direct, and trust as naturally as they'd work with a great colleague. Nobody has solved the design problems in between.

The surfaces where enterprises build, control, and come to trust autonomous agents don't have established patterns yet, and this role exists to invent them. This is an opportunity to define what great agent UX looks like, across chat, voice, and the interfaces behind authoring those agents.
In this role, you will
As an early and senior member of the design team, you'll work across several areas of the product and own initiatives end to end, from discovery and scoping through launch and adoption. The work often starts before the problem is defined.

You'll turn ambiguity into clarity, framing the problem space before jumping to solutions, and you'll design concepts that balance vision, craft, speed, and business potential. You'll guide decisions with structured thinking and clearly articulated design rationale.
We work in small, autonomous project teams where designers pair tightly with engineers and product managers. You'll interview customers, translate what you learn into the roadmap, and ship: polished new features, meaningful refinements to key flows, and along the way, build the foundational design systems that help us move faster.

Fluency with AI coding tools is part design craft here. You'll prototype in Figma and in AI tools like Cursor and Claude Code, building directly on our codebase to make design ideas real enough to critique. And as a founding member of our growing design team, you'll shape our culture, hiring, and ways of working.

About Halter
At Halter, we’re on a mission to enable farmers and graziers to run the most productive and sustainable operations. Our customers are using Halter to break free from the time-intensive constraints of conventional practices. Imagine watching 500 cattle stand up and walk calmly towards their next break? No quad bikes, no dogs, no fences.

Just a group of cattle walking at their own pace. People say it looks like magic. Our customers are revolutionizing grazing with Halter. It's changing lives and transforming an industry. People join Halter to do meaningful work. By joining us you’ll be solving challenging problems within a talented team and a culture built for high performance.

Our team out-think, out-work and out-care. We’re committed to delivering real change in the world - this isn’t easy, and in truth, we love that it’s hard.
We’re backed to deliver on a mission that matters by Tier 1 investors including Founders Fund , Bessemer Venture Partners , BOND, DCVC , Blackbird , Promus Ventures , Rocket Lab’s Peter Beck and Icehouse ventures .
To find out more, visit our LinkedIn & Instagram .

How do you represent a living, literally breathing farm in an app and then let someone control it from their pocket?
With Halter's solar-powered collars and software, farmers can fence and shift cattle, manage their pasture and the environment more effectively and monitor animal health, all from one app in real time. There is no reference for this, no pattern library, no interaction models to borrow from. We are inventing them.
A farm is alive and always moving: animals, pasture, weather, all changing by the minute. Our job is to turn that into something a farmer can read at a glance and act on with total confidence. The stakes are physical and the visual and interaction bar is extremely high, this is a farmer's entire farm in their pocket, it should feel like it. Beautifully crafted and a joy to use, every day, for years.
We're looking for a Staff Product Designer to lead the design of a significant area of the product experience at Halter. You'll take on some of our hardest problems and help set the bar for what Halter's product experience should feel like.
Design at Halter is high agency and high impact. We help define what we should build and why, we spend real time with farmers, ranchers and graziers in the field, and we shape where Halter goes next.
This role is based in our Auckland, New Zealand HQ, relocation and visa assistance is provided.

Set, own and advance our design foundations across mobile and web.
Set the standard for craft at Halter, and make that standard usable through principles, guidance and worked examples that raise the quality of what every team ships.
Shape the technical architecture and system structure alongside engineers.
Treat the system as a product with real customers. Set its direction, prioritise what to build next based on what designers and engineers actually need.
Give teams a clear point of view on which pattern to reach for and why.
Turn our field conditions into standards the system carries by default: legibility, target sizes, clarity at a glance.
Work alongside teams to spot what's working across new product surfaces and promote it into documented, reusable foundations. Decide what earns the right to be a pattern and what's better left a considered one-off.
Raise the craft of the designers around you through feedback, reviews and mentorship, and champion the system across product, engineering and design leadership.

8+ years designing digital products, with significant time spent designing and building design systems at scale.
Exceptional visual craft and command of typography, layout, spacing, colour, accessibility, interaction and motion design.
Proven experience shipping a design system with engineers. You know how tokens and component libraries are structured in code, and you've built and maintained the Figma to code connection.
A portfolio showing both foundational systems work, and concrete high-craft experiences built with it.
Not just taste, but conviction and the language to make your judgment explicit, teachable and useful to others.
A track record of coaching other designers and raising quality around you, and the presence to build alignment and defend an opinionated decision.

Delicious snacks and drinks are available for your daily flow.
Healthy body, healthy mind. We're partnered with Southern Cross Health Insurance to support your well-being.
We offer 6 months of fully paid parental leave for primary caregivers, 4 weeks of fully paid secondary caregiver leave and many other parental benefits that support you and your family.
Our personal growth is important. Halter offers an annual $1000 self-development budget to be used for anything that fuels personal growth.
Our time to recharge is valued, we're offered wellness leave and unlimited paid annual leave.
Importantly, we offer an inclusive and attractive remuneration package made up of salary, benefits and an employee stock ownership plan.
Our Office First Approach
Humans are wired for connection. Being office first is a core pillar of our culture because in-person connections drive your growth, learning, impact, and relationships. Strong relationships make it easier to disagree, give feedback, and do meaningful work together.
We're office first, not office only. Working from the office is our default, but we flex when needed. We have a high-trust culture where everyone is trusted to do what's best for Halter.
Our office vibe is special, the high energy and spectacular people make work enjoyable. Your growth and impact are unlimited here, coming from solving problems, innovating, and constantly learning from each other.
Join our team
Halter is committed to promoting a diverse and inclusive workplace — a place where we can each be ourselves and do the best work of our lives. Research shows that while men apply to jobs when they meet an average of 60% of the requirements, women and under-represented groups of candidates tend to only apply when they meet every requirement.

If you think you have what it takes but don’t necessarily tick every requirement on this job description, please still get in touch and apply to Halter. We’d love to chat to see if you’ll be an epic fit!
If this opportunity sounds like you, please apply below by sending through your cover letter explaining why you’re excited about this role and working at Halter, along with your CV, and we’ll be in touch!
Please also feel free to check out the careers page for more information on working at Halter and don't forget to follow us on LinkedIn & Instagram .

This is a strategic and hands-on role. You’ll contribute to the future direction of our growth experiences while continuously identifying opportunities to improve what exists today. You’ll work in an AI-native design environment , using AI throughout the design lifecycle to accelerate discovery, synthesis, prototyping, and execution — while applying strong judgment around where AI improves the quality of the customer experience.
At Senior level, we expect you to independently lead ambiguous product challenges, influence product direction, and contribute patterns and practices that make the broader team stronger. You’ll remain deeply involved in the craft, using the quality of your thinking, design, and collaboration to bring others along.

Lead high-impact Growth experiences
Own the end-to-end design of critical growth journeys across acquisition, conversion, checkout, payment, reactivation, and emerging purchase models.
Translate complex customer and business problems into experiences that clearly communicate value, reduce friction, and help customers confidently make decisions.
Balance immediate conversion opportunities with the longer-term customer experience, considering not only whether customers convert, but whether we are setting them up for meaningful engagement and retention.
Shape product direction
Partner with Product, Engineering, Data, Research, Marketing, and Content Design to identify opportunities across the customer journey.
Connect customer needs, behavioural insights, commercial goals, and emerging technology to develop strong product directions.
Move comfortably between contributing to longer-term vision and delivering tactical improvements that generate measurable impact today.
Bring a strong design perspective to your product area while remaining open to evidence, experimentation, and the expertise of your partners.
Drive experimentation and validated learning
Use quantitative and qualitative insights to identify opportunities, develop hypotheses, and design high-impact experiments.
Partner closely with Product and Data to understand performance across the funnel and translate learnings into actionable design improvements.
Look beyond the outcome of individual A/B tests to identify patterns and insights that can inform future product and design decisions.
Help teams balance experimentation velocity with customer comprehension, trust, and experience quality.
Work AI-natively
Integrate AI into your day-to-day design practice, from exploration, research synthesis, and ideation through rapid prototyping and design-to-code workflows.
Use tools such as Claude & Claude Code, Gemini, Figma AI, and emerging technologies to shorten the distance between an idea and something customers can experience and validate.
Explore opportunities for AI-native customer experiences, including personalization, recommendations, adaptive journeys, and conversational interactions.
Apply strong design judgment to AI-generated outputs, understanding when AI accelerates quality and when human craft, intuition, and critical thinking matter most.
Raise the bar for design craft
Create polished, intuitive experiences with strong attention to visual hierarchy, interaction design, motion, micro-interactions, content, and overall usability.
Identify opportunities to improve the quality and coherence of the Growth experiences you work on.
Contribute patterns, practices, and examples that help other designers deliver stronger work.
Give and seek thoughtful critique, using feedback to continuously strengthen the work.
Design systems, not just screens
Think across journeys rather than individual touchpoints, identifying opportunities to create reusable patterns and modular experiences that can scale across markets, brands, customer types, and purchase models.
Partner with our design system teams while contributing to Growth-specific patterns where needed.
Help reduce design debt and fragmentation by creating solutions that make future experimentation faster without sacrificing relevance or quality.
Lead through collaboration
Bring strong perspectives and clear rationale to complex product decisions.
Guide cross-functional partners through ambiguity and trade-offs, advocating for customer-centred solutions while understanding commercial and technical constraints.
Build alignment through clear communication, evidence, and strong design rationale rather than formal authority.
Support other designers through critique, collaboration, and sharing new practices and approaches.

Senior-level product design experience
Typically 4-6+ years of product design experience , although we care more about the scope, complexity, and impact of your work than years alone.
A strong portfolio demonstrating end-to-end ownership of complex consumer experiences, from understanding the problem through shipped outcomes and learning.
Experience independently navigating ambiguous problems, making sound design decisions, and influencing product direction within your area.
Growth and experimentation expertise
Strong experience designing B2C growth, e-commerce, subscription, marketplace, or other transaction-driven experiences.
You understand experimentation deeply and can translate behavioural data, customer insights, and business metrics into meaningful design opportunities.
You know how to optimize for conversion without losing sight of trust, comprehension, customer value, and longer-term engagement.
Exceptional product design craft
Strong expertise across interaction and visual design, including hierarchy, information architecture, responsive behaviour, motion, and micro-interactions.
You can take complex experiences and make them feel simple, and can articulate what separates a functional experience from a great one.
You care about the details while understanding when speed, learning, and iteration matter more than perfection.
AI-native design fluency
AI is already part of how you work, not something you are waiting to adopt.
You regularly use AI across multiple stages of your design process, whether that’s discovery, synthesis, ideation, prototyping, or execution.
You’re comfortable experimenting with tools such as Figma AI, Claude, Claude Code, Gemini, or similar emerging technologies.
You’re interested not only in using AI to work faster, but in understanding how it changes what we can design for customers.
Systems thinking
You naturally look beyond the individual screen or experiment to understand how experiences connect.
